correctness.rationale: PASS: Each tetrahedron of C_m*C_n induces one double edge between same-factor cycle edges and two cross-factor opposite-edge pairs, proving D²(X)=K_m,n disjoint union categorical C_m×C_n. The latter is connected whenever at least one polygon length is odd. Removing a tetrahedron leaves each of its two graph pieces connected because K_m,n loses one edge and the two removed categorical product edges admit 3-edge detours (m,n>=4). The six double boundary vertices form a two-port same-factor block and four-port cross block on each side. Eight tetrahedral bijections preserve their marked perfect matching, giving two glued components; the other 16 mix ports and merge all four pieces. Vertex/edge subtraction gives ranks (2mn−2m−2n+1,2mn+1) or 4mn−2m−2n+1, with the stated equal f-vector. Independent combinatorial enumeration of all 24 twists at (4,5) reproduced 8 two-component / 16 one-component cases, graph ranks (23,41) versus 63; analytic graph construction and gluing proof cover arbitrary admissible m,n.
